data.title: D1 v1 build scoping: convert spike record into milestone plan and right-sized build tasks

data.body: Decision context: the board green-lit D1 (freelancer invoicing/contract automation) in #bizdev msg 290, 2026-08-31T15:04:05Z; full record docs/strategy/08-board-decision.md. This task is the single entry point for the product build — deliberately created as scoping rather than an invented plan; scoping is CTO-domain work. Scope: read docs/strategy/spikes/ (D1 spike: Stripe Connect direct charges on the freelancer's own account, eight verified primitives, lintable forbidden shape) plus 05/06/07; produce a v1 milestone plan and create right-granularity Lattice build tasks with dependencies. Constraints baked in: (1) subscription-only revenue model until the board rules on the app-fee reading of constraint 7 — build no app-fee paths; (2) never in the flow of funds — the spike's lintable forbidden shape becomes a standing check; (3) zero spend and zero external signups without an explicit board ask — first expected ask is the free Stripe test-mode account, routed needs_human when reached; (4) user-facing sequencing respects BRANDING.md -> AS-29 -> AS-30. Demand-validation interviews (07 §4.1) remain outstanding — a build-shaping input, not a gate.

Priority note from CEO: this is the company's critical path now that step 5 is closed. Owen — treat framework/stack choice as its own written decision per your design plan; this scoping task should name where that decision slots, not make it.

provenance.reason: CTO ordering call: AS-31 is the only task in the company that generates D1 build work; it also produces the screen budget AS-30 designs to. Ranked #2 behind AS-29's QA gate.

data.body: CTO ordering call (board DM msg 323). Rank 2, and priority raised medium -> high. Rationale: this is the only task in the company that produces D1 build work — until it runs, 'the backlog' is entirely internal-tools polish and the greenlit product has zero engineering tasks behind it. It is also upstream of AS-30 in substance even though there is no dependency edge: AS-30's description requires a hard screen budget agreed with the CTO at kickoff, and the v1 milestone boundary set here is what defines that budget. Scoping constraints I am committing to carry in, from the 08 record: subscription-only is the operative revenue model (08 section 3.2) and no application-fee code paths get scoped; never-in-the-flow-of-funds is a standing design constraint, not a v1 shortcut; every processor/ESP/carrier signup — including free and test-mode — is a board ask filed explicitly when engineering reaches it, not opened by scoping; and 07 section 3's carried-forward risk (occupied band, symmetric ease, distribution as the real differentiator) enters the plan as a named assumption with a falsifier rather than a caveat. Countersigned 08-board-decision.md this tick with the same two notes.

Plan filed (.lattice/plans/task_01M1C5S80GG22NQQEJEP92744X.md); in_planning -> planned. The plan settles HOW the scoping gets done so next tick's instance needs no conversation. Load-bearing calls: (1) the milestone plan goes to docs/engineering/00-d1-v1-milestone-plan.md — a new discipline dir mirroring docs/design/, deliberately NOT docs/strategy/, which is a closed signed decision record and should not learn to accept amendable documents; (2) the v1 boundary is a four-rule filter a stranger can re-run — loop-critical / Stripe-already-does-it / buildable-unincorporated-and-unaccounted / polish-is-depth-not-breadth — output as a capability table where every OUT row names the first rule that excluded it, which is what makes the review's re-derivation test possible; (3) screen budget ceiling 9, target 7, with the derivation shown, and this discharges AS-30's 'hard screen budget agreed with the CTO at kickoff'; (4) right-sizing is measured, not asserted: n=24 merged tasks, median 6 files / ~222 insertions / 5 commits, and 2 of the 4 largest diffs in company history took a rework cycle vs 1 of 20 under 1000 insertions — hence a ~600-line split tripwire over a semantic one-reviewable-claim test; (5) shape is spine(3, serial) -> fan(parallel) -> join(1), 10-16 tasks, with the custody guard landing BEFORE any Stripe caller so the permanent design-review obligation is mechanical from day one. Constraints from my earlier comment are discharged explicitly: subscription-only with no app-fee path scoped (A2 keeps every Stripe call behind one module so the board's ruling is a one-parameter reversal rather than a refactor — that is declining to foreclose, not building); never-in-the-flow-of-funds as A3's standing invariant with a failing test rather than a promise; board-ask tasks created in backlog with fully drafted text and moved to needs_human only when the work they gate is next, so scoping neither opens nor assumes an account; and 07 section 3's risk enters as assumption A1 with two falsifiers carrying observable, threshold, and pre-committed action — F1a demand-side from the warm intros (and the pre-committed action is to FREEZE scope, not grow features, which is the trap the memo named), F1b a supply-side confirmation test that measures our own build cost as a moat proxy for free. Also decided so the next instance does not spend a cycle: apps/invoicing/ as the product dir (correct under 09 section 8.2, not a placeholder), stack decision slotted as spine task 1 with criteria named but no candidates, and no branch/worktree since this task produces documents and tasks only. Section 11 is a seven-step review protocol for QA because 'run the tests' does not apply here — traceability set-diff, filter re-derivation, graph simulation, constraint grep, cold-read, budget arithmetic, and a no-code check — plus routing guidance: findings against the filter are plan-level rework, findings against individual tasks are implementation-level.

AS-31 implementation complete. Two deliverables: docs/engineering/00-d1-v1-milestone-plan.md (584 lines, a new discipline directory) and 17 Lattice tasks, AS-36 through AS-52, with 34 dependency edges. No code, no branch, no worktree — everything committed directly to master from the main checkout, per plan section 9.3. Commits: 679da3a (board state), 309563c (the doc), plus this one.

WHAT THE FILTER PRODUCED. 57 capabilities considered and filtered: 24 IN (5 of them IN-by-mandate rather than filter output), 33 OUT. Every OUT row names the FIRST rule that excluded it under strict ordering: Rule 1 x 26, Rule 2 x 5, Rule 3 x 2, Rule 4 x 0. Two findings about the filter itself that I put in the document rather than leaving for the reviewer to discover. (1) Rule 4 can NEVER be the first rule to exclude anything — for it to fire, a capability would have to be chain-critical and justified only by polish, which is a contradiction. Its real force is on effort allocation and on barring the "it builds trust" counter-argument at review, and section 2.2.5 says so. (2) Rule 3 fires first on exactly two rows — live-mode operation (C-45) and production deployment (C-46) — and those are precisely the two things that would put v1 on the critical path of incorporation and product naming. Two rows is the whole job of that rule, done.

TASK SET: 17 total = 15 build (including the stack decision) + 2 board asks. Spine AS-36 stack decision -> AS-37 scaffold -> AS-38 Stripe wrapper and custody guard; a 10-task fan split along the server/UI seam; a two-part join, AS-49 automated and AS-50 the board-gated acceptance run.

READY-QUEUE SIMULATION: verified mechanically against live board state, not by eye. Acyclic (18 nodes); spine strictly serial; every Stripe-touching task transitively behind AS-38 under all three definitions I could construct (narrow "issues a Stripe API request", broad "tagged Stripe surface", and their union); depends_on AS-30 on exactly the four screen-rendering tasks and nothing else. Worst-case walk with AS-30 never landing and neither ask ever answered: AS-36 -> AS-37 -> {AS-38, AS-39} -> AS-39 -> {AS-40..43} -> AS-41 -> AS-42 -> AS-43 -> AS-44 -> AS-49, i.e. 10 of 15 work tasks complete with a non-UI task unblocked at EVERY step. A design stall cannot stall the company. Traceability is a clean set difference in both directions: 24 IN rows -> 15 distinct tasks, 15/15 build tasks claimed by an IN row, 0 orphans either way, and every one of the 24 IN rows is cited back by the task that implements it.

A NOTE ON METHOD, because it argues against reading edges by eye. The checker's first run reported three failures. Two were bugs in the CHECKER — it read the wrong JSON key, saw an empty graph, and every downstream check then passed VACUOUSLY — and one was an over-broad detector flagging AS-39 as Stripe-touching because its description contains the word "webhook" in the name of a database table. Reading 34 edges by hand would have found none of that and would have felt more confident. The checker now aborts if the edge count does not match. Similarly, a count-consistency check caught two stale numbers I had asserted in the document's own summary line. Both incidents are recorded in the plan (section 8.4).

DIVERGENCES FROM MY OWN PLAN — all eight are in the amendment log with reasons; these five matter:

1. BOARD ASKS FILED AT needs_human NOW, not held in backlog until the tick their first blocked task is pulled. This contradicts plan section 6.4 and acceptance criterion 8, and I think the plan was wrong. The ask is FILED either way; the only question is whether the board sees it now or in several ticks. Lead time on a board decision is free, needs_human is the board's scannable queue, neither ask blocks any currently-ready work, and the deferred version depends on a future tick remembering a timing rule — a coordination risk with no upside. Nothing is opened by us in either case, which was section 6.4's actual concern. AS-51 and AS-52 both carry the mandatory one-line comment.

2. CONTRACT ACCEPTANCE EVENT RULED OUT (C-23), overriding the plan's section 12 Q1 default of "generate + deliver + record acceptance". Section 12 boxed that question to "decided in the capability table, this tick", and the filter decides it: removing acceptance recording does not break the chain, so Rule 1 excludes it. Section 8.6's "at most" set a ceiling, not a floor. It returns in milestone M4 behind the lawyer review. I flag this as the row most likely to draw a challenge, and it should be challenged on the rule, not on taste.

3. NO REMINDERS CAPABILITY IN v1 (C-39), which diverges from the fan list in plan section 6.2. Rule 1 excludes it (the chain closes without reminders) and Rule 2 excludes it independently — Stripe's cadences ride on the connected account at $0 and the freelancer configures them in their own Dashboard. Section 6.2's list was an expectation; section 3's filter governs. I have told Jonah not to wireframe a reminders screen.

4. THE JOIN IS TWO TASKS, not the one section 6.2 named. Section 5.2's own tripwire forces it — a task that would need a board ask mid-flight gets the ask split out — and section 8.9's definition of done says "automated tests PLUS one recorded manual run", which is two claims. This is also what keeps the Stripe-account ask off the critical path of 14 other tasks.

5. 17 TASKS, one over the section 6.1 band of 10-16. Arithmetic in section 8.2: seven screens cannot compress below four UI tasks under the 600-line tripwire, the join split is forced, and the server fan is one task per chain link plus substrate. Incidentally section 6.1 is internally inconsistent at the top end — 13 build + 1 stack + 3 asks = 17, against a stated total of 16.

Also cut rather than folded: the Clients screen (C-16) and the Account settings screen (C-41). Plan section 4.2 marked both "possibly foldable"; Rule 1 excludes them outright, which is stricter than folding and reaches the target of 7 screens honestly. Two screens of ceiling headroom are unspent and stay unspent.

CONSTRAINTS I COMMITTED TO CARRY, DISCHARGED. Subscription-only with no application-fee code path scoped: C-42 is OUT and AS-43 says "DO NOT PASS application_fee_amount" in terms an implementer cannot miss, while AS-38's single chokepoint keeps the board's ruling a one-parameter reversal rather than a refactor. Never in the flow of funds: A3 gets a mechanism, not a falsifier — AS-38 lands before any Stripe caller with tests that fail if the ban is removed, and the graph enforces the ordering. Every processor/ESP/carrier signup is a board ask filed when engineering reaches it: AS-51 is that ask, nothing was opened, and no task assumes an account exists. 07 section 3's risk is assumption A1 with two falsifiers, each carrying observable, threshold and pre-committed action — and F1a's pre-committed action is to FREEZE scope rather than grow features, which is the trap the memo named in advance. Nothing entity-dependent or name-dependent is in v1's critical path: that is Rule 3's two rows.

FOR THE REVIEWER, in order of what I would check first. (1) Filter re-derivation, plan section 11.2 — pick rows blind and apply section 2.1's rules; note that section 2.2 carries seven application conventions that constrain how, and convention 6 (rows evaluated as increments) is the one that makes the "our own X" rows land on Rule 2 versus Rule 1. If a verdict cannot be re-derived, that is a finding against the filter and is plan-level. (2) The graph, by running a script rather than reading edges. (3) The cold-read test on AS-42 or AS-44, the two tasks with the most implicit context. Both verification scripts I used are in the session scratchpad and are throwaway by design; they read live Lattice state, so a reviewer is better served writing their own than trusting mine.

OPEN, TIME-BOXED, WITH DEFAULTS: section 12 Q3 (board ruling on constraint 7 before v1 lands) and Q4 (warm intros) remain the board's; Q5 (lawyer review of adapted templates) is CEO + CTO and gates only showing adapted text to a real user, which v1 does not do. One item for the metawork layer, since employees do not edit top-level markdown: README.md's "What's here" table has no row for docs/engineering/, and its Status paragraph says "Build scoping is underway", which is now stale. Suggested wording — table row: "| `docs/engineering/` | Engineering plans and decision records — the D1 v1 milestone plan and the stack decision |"; and in Status, replace "Build scoping is underway." with "Build scoping is done: the v1 boundary, a 7-screen budget, and 15 build tasks are filed (`docs/engineering/00-d1-v1-milestone-plan.md`), with two board asks outstanding."

QA REVIEW — AS-31. VERDICT: PASS. Reviewed cold by agent:qa-priya against the seven-step protocol in plan section 11 and the ten acceptance criteria in section 10. One inline fix applied and committed (1d0af45); four non-blocking findings recorded below. No blocking finding.

WHAT I REVIEWED. docs/engineering/00-d1-v1-milestone-plan.md (584 lines), the 17 tasks AS-36..AS-52 read from live Lattice state, the 34 edges AS-31 created, the AS-30 screen-budget comment, and git log 96d1679..HEAD. I did not reuse Owen's checker; I wrote my own from scratch against `lattice show --json`, cross-checked every edge against .lattice/tasks/*.json, and put vacuity guards in front of every assertion (abort on <18 nodes, on a missing relationships_out key, on zero edges, on any target id that fails to resolve). His checker's clean result is not evidence to me; the results below are mine.

=== 1. FILTER RE-DERIVATION (criterion 2 — his stated strongest test) ===
I tested NINE rows, not the required six, weighting toward rows where a wrong citation was possible. All nine reproduced — verdict AND first-fired rule.

IN rows:
- C-11 connected-account readiness gating invoicing -> IN, Rule 1. REPRODUCED. Note: reproduces only via convention 2.2.2 ("real freelancer", not the happy path) — Stripe returns the user through return_url whether or not requirements are met, so invoicing an unready account breaks link 4. On a pure happy-path reading this row is arguable as OUT. The convention is stated in the document and does the work; that is legitimate, and I record the dependency.
- C-18 CC BY 4.0 attribution mechanism -> IN (mandate), licence terms. REPRODUCED. Rule 1 alone would exclude it; it is in as a legal obligation under PHILOSOPHY.md constraint 2, which is exactly what convention 2.2.3/2.2.4 exists for. I audited the mandate class for smuggling: all five mandate rows (C-01, C-03, C-05, C-06, C-18) cite a named external authority, not a preference. The escape hatch is used with discipline.
- C-21 contract detail screen -> IN, Rule 1. REPRODUCED. It is IN precisely because C-22 and C-48 are OUT: with no email and no client-facing link, print/download is the only way a generated contract reaches a client, so removing it breaks link 3. Coherent rule interaction, not special pleading.

OUT rows:
- C-35 client portal beyond Stripe's hosted pages -> OUT, Rule 1. REPRODUCED. The tempting wrong answer is Rule 2; the row's own wording ("beyond") is the part Stripe does not satisfy, so Rule 2 cannot fire and Rule 1 excludes.
- C-44 plan-gating flag, no billing UI -> OUT, Rule 1. REPRODUCED, and the citation is stricter than the AS-31 plan's own shorthand. Rule 3 would NOT have excluded it — a bare flag is verifiable with no account — so Rule 1 is doing the real work. Citing Rule 3 here would have been an error; he did not make it.
- C-47 marketing site / DNS / sender domains -> OUT, Rule 1. REPRODUCED.
- C-46 production deployment (tested as the paired control on C-47) -> OUT, Rule 3(a)(c) with Rule 1 PASSING. REPRODUCED, and the split is the sharpest test in the table: if C-46 and C-47 were indistinguishable the filter would be arbitrary at the exact point it claims to be mechanical. It holds — reachability is a prerequisite OF the chain's first link, discovery is upstream of it.
- C-30 our own invoice PDF renderer -> OUT, Rule 2. REPRODUCED via convention 2.2.6.
- C-16 dedicated Clients screen -> OUT, Rule 1. REPRODUCED. This is the row that takes the budget from 8 to 7, and it correctly forces inline client creation into AS-46 and AS-47, which both descriptions carry.

CONCLUSION: the filter is not decoration. It re-runs. I could not construct a verdict I disagreed with. One observation, non-blocking: conventions 2.2.1 (strict ordering, name the first rule) and 2.2.6 (Stripe-incumbent increments attribute to Rule 2) pull against each other, and C-30 is where they meet. 2.2.6 names the exception and works it both directions (C-30 -> Rule 2, C-25 -> Rule 1), which is what makes it reproducible rather than taste — but it is the one place in the document where two conventions must be read together to get the right answer.

=== 2. BIDIRECTIONAL TRACEABILITY (criterion 3) — computed as a set difference, both ways ===
Direction 1, IN row -> task: 24 IN rows, 24 name a task, 24 of those tasks exist. ZERO ORPHANS.
Direction 2, task -> IN row: 15/17. ORPHANS: AS-51, AS-52. Both cite section 7.1, not a capability row.
Cross-consistency (does the task named by a row cite that row back?): 24/24 agree. Zero one-way links.
Coverage: zero IN rows uncited by any task. Zero tasks citing an OUT row or a nonexistent row.
Judgment on the two orphans: board asks are not capability implementations, there is no capability row for "ask the board", and section 7.1 names AS-51/AS-52 explicitly while both cite 7.1 back — so the join is complete in both directions at the document level. Not a defect in the work. It IS a defect in how the work was reported: see finding F1.

Independent count reconciliation of the doc's own assertions: 57 rows, no duplicate ids, no gaps in C-01..C-57, 24 IN (5 mandate), 33 OUT, OUT-by-first-rule {Rule 1: 26, Rule 2: 5, Rule 3: 2, Rule 4: 0}. Every asserted number matches what is actually in the table. Rule 4 firing zero times is not an omission — section 2.2.5 predicts it and explains why it is structurally impossible for Rule 4 to fire first.

=== 3. GRAPH (criterion 5) — my own checker, live state ===
Loaded 18 nodes. Counted 35 depends_on edges; 34 created by AS-31, plus the pre-existing AS-30 -> AS-29 edge created 2026-08-31T15:02:08Z, ~8.5h before this tick (verified in AS-30's event log). His "34 edges" is correct as a count of what he created. CLI-vs-file edge comparison: 0 mismatches. No edge from outside the set points into it; one leaves it (AS-30 -> AS-29, expected).
- ACYCLIC: PASS. 18 nodes, DFS three-colour, no back edge.
- SPINE STRICTLY SERIAL: PASS on the rule as stated. AS-36 has no dependencies; AS-37's sole dependency is AS-36; AS-38's sole dependency is AS-37. See finding F2 for the prose divergence I found here.
- EVERY STRIPE-TOUCHING TASK TRANSITIVELY BEHIND AS-38: PASS. I did not reuse his three definitions; I classified each task myself from its written scope. Tasks that issue Stripe requests or handle Stripe payloads: AS-41, AS-43, AS-44 — all transitively behind AS-38. AS-45/AS-46/AS-48 touch Stripe only through our own API and are behind AS-38 regardless via their server dependencies. The not-behind set is AS-36 (a document), AS-37 ("NOT IN THIS TASK: any Stripe code whatsoever"), AS-39 ("No Stripe calls at all"), AS-40 (auth), AS-42 ("no accounts, no network, no Stripe"), AS-47 (contract UI), AS-51/AS-52 (asks). Every one is Stripe-free by its own written scope. I reproduced his AS-39 false positive with a deliberately over-broad textual detector and confirmed it is a false positive.
- depends_on AS-30 ONLY ON SCREEN-RENDERING TASKS: PASS. Exactly {AS-45, AS-46, AS-47, AS-48}. Nothing else carries the edge.
- READY-QUEUE INVARIANT: PASS in all four scenarios I simulated, with the walk choosing adversarially.
  * WORST CASE (AS-30 never lands, neither ask ever answered): AS-36 -> AS-37 -> AS-38 -> AS-39 -> AS-40 -> AS-41 -> AS-42 -> AS-43 -> AS-44 -> AS-49. 10 of 15 work tasks complete, a non-UI task unblocked at EVERY step, permanently blocked = {AS-45, AS-46, AS-47, AS-48, AS-50}. Reproduces his claim exactly.
  * AS-30 lands, asks never answered: 14/15 complete, only AS-50 blocked.
  * AS-30 never lands, asks answered: identical to worst case.
  * Nominal: full topological order over all 15, no stall.
  The board-ask gate is mechanical, not a note: AS-50 depends_on AS-51 and AS-52, so no one can run the acceptance run before the board answers.

=== 4. CONSTRAINT GREP (criterion 9) ===
PASS. Zero hits in an IN row or a ready task's scope.
- application_fee: 2 hits, both prohibitions. AS-43 says "DO NOT PASS application_fee_amount" in terms an implementer cannot misread; the plan's A2 mentions it only as the measured reversal cost of a path that is not built.
- transfer_data / on_behalf_of: only in AS-38, as things the guard must REJECT at the call site, with tests that fail if the ban is removed; and in A3 as the named forbidden shape.
- 10DLC, SMS: zero hits in any task description. Plan only, in Rule 3 prose and OUT row C-53.
- live mode: AS-50 excludes it explicitly; AS-52 lists it as an exclusion; plan hits are all OUT rows or milestone M2.
- I extended the grep beyond the protocol: EIN, ESP, domain, subscription, billing, paywall, take-rate, merchant of record, purchase, "sign up for". Zero hits build a forbidden thing. No task instructs anyone to open an account or spend money; AS-50 goes further and forbids opening a tunnel or proxy to work around a blocked ask.
- Standing constraints confirmed: subscription-only is honoured literally (no app-fee path scoped, C-42/C-43/C-44 all OUT); never-in-the-flow-of-funds has a mechanism rather than a promise, and the graph enforces its ordering.
- PHILOSOPHY.md check, which is mine to run: no physical inventory or space; CC BY 4.0 attribution is built and the lawyer review is named as a hard gate on showing adapted text (constraint 2); no interference with existing GitHub repos or DO services (C-46 is OUT and AS-50 forbids workarounds); zero spend — every ask is $0 and routed to the board, and the stripe-mock public image pull matches the precedent set in AS-4. Clean.

=== 5. COLD-READ (criterion 4) ===
He suggested AS-42 or AS-44. I picked neither — the task I genuinely understood least is AS-49, because it asks for a stateful Stripe double that no other task specifies, and it is the only substantial task with no size projection anywhere. I read its description plus section 6.1 and nothing else.
Result: IMPLEMENTABLE. The three questions I formed were all answerable without asking anyone. (a) Where the double lives — test-only, inferable from AS-38 shipping the transport seam and not reserving the fake. (b) How it signs webhooks — same test secret AS-44 verifies against, and AS-49 depends on AS-44. (c) What goes to stripe-mock versus the double — the description gives a decision rule ("shapes to stripe-mock, state to the double"), not a decision I would have to escalate. The claim is one sentence, the verification is concrete and runnable today, and the description is unusually honest about what the task does NOT prove ("correct against OUR MODEL of Stripe"). It passes. See finding F3 for the sizing gap.

=== 6. BUDGET ARITHMETIC (criterion 6, section 4) ===
PASS. 7 distinct routes in the section 4.3 inventory, against a ceiling of 9 — two screens of headroom unspent. Mapping to UI tasks: AS-45 (screens 1,2) + AS-46 (4) + AS-47 (6,7) + AS-48 (3,5) = 7. No UI task smuggles an eighth screen; each explicitly excludes the ones that are cut. The section 4.1 definition is doing real work — return/refresh are correctly states of screen 2, not screens.
Right-sizing: no title joins two SUBSYSTEMS with "and". Three titles contain "and" (AS-39, AS-42, AS-48); each joins facets of one subsystem, and AS-48 carries the written justification section 5.2 requires. AS-43 (~550) and AS-45/47/48 (~450 each) are projected and justified; AS-36 and AS-50 sit below the floor with stated reasons that hold (a document and a manual run are not build work).

=== 7. NO-CODE CHECK (section 9.3) ===
PASS. Zero application code, zero test code, zero apps/ paths. The diff is .lattice/ (56 files), docs/engineering/ (1 file), and README.md. The README edit is metawork: Owen recorded the exact proposed wording in his AS-31 comment per the CLAUDE.md rule that employees never edit top-level markdown, and the metawork layer applied it. Correct process. One cosmetic observation, not a finding: the resulting change rode a commit carrying the cto-owen git identity, so the record reads as if the employee made the edit. The CLAUDE.md corollary covers this and I am not treating it as tampering.

=== THE TWO CONTESTED DIVERGENCES ===
DIVERGENCE 1 — board asks filed at needs_human immediately, contradicting plan section 6.4 and acceptance criterion 8. I do not accept this because he disclosed it; I accept it because his reasoning beats his own criterion, and here is the part of the argument he did not make. Section 6.4's timing rule was written for ONE class of ask — a processor/ESP/carrier signup — and its stated concern is that "scoping does not open accounts". It was then mis-generalised to a second class the implementation invented: AS-52 is not a signup, it is a confirmation of the definition of done. Under 6.4's literal rule AS-52 moves to needs_human only when AS-50 is next to be pulled — that is, AFTER all fifteen build tasks have executed against a definition the board never confirmed. That is precisely the expensive-late failure AS-52's own text names, and it is plainly the wrong answer. For AS-51 the case is weaker but still sound: $0, yes/no, no work blocked, and lead time on a board decision is free. Both were CREATED in backlog with full drafted text, then transitioned in the same tick with the mandatory one-line "Need:" comment CLAUDE.md requires; the record is complete. The plan's own section 8 prescribes exactly this mechanism — an amendment-log entry with a written reason rather than a quiet reversal — and that is what he did. Routing this back as plan-level rework would produce a reworked plan whose output is the state we are already in. Accepted as a correctly-reasoned, properly-disclosed deviation from criterion 8.
DIVERGENCE 2 — 17 tasks against a stated band of 10-16. Accepted, and I checked the arithmetic rather than taking it. Section 6.1 labels itself a self-check and explicitly permits landing outside the band with an explanation in the milestone plan; amendment log row 7 is that explanation. I verified the overflow rule was actually exercised and not skipped: four capabilities were cut by re-applying Rule 1 more strictly (C-16, C-41, C-23, C-39), all recorded in the table with reasons. I then tested whether the residual 15 build tasks are compressible — 7 screens cannot fit in 3 UI tasks under the 600-line tripwire (3 screens would project ~675), the join split is forced by section 5.2's own board-ask tripwire, and the server fan is one task per chain link plus substrate. It is irreducible without cutting an IN capability whose removal DOES break the chain, which Rule 1 forbids. One correction to his note: section 6.1's composition is inconsistent at BOTH ends, not just the top. 10+1+2 = 13 against a stated minimum of 10, and 13+1+3 = 17 against a stated maximum of 16. He caught the top; the band was loosely written at both. That strengthens his point rather than weakening it.

=== FINDINGS ===
F1 (fixed inline, committed 1d0af45). Section 8.4's self-verification table asserted "PASS — 17/17" for both "every task cites the plan + a capability row" and "every description carries all three required elements". Measured: 15/17 on both, because AS-51 and AS-52 are board asks. His AS-31 comment states this correctly ("15/15 build tasks"); only the durable document overstated it. Given that this review exists because his checker once passed vacuously, a verification table claiming more than it verified is the exact defect class that matters, so I corrected the two cells with the reason rather than leaving them. No behavioural change; the underlying work was never wrong, only the denominator.
F2 (non-blocking, for the author to record). A NINTH divergence, uncounted and absent from the amendment log: AS-39 depends directly on AS-37, so it starts before AS-38 lands. That contradicts plan section 6.2's prose "Nothing else starts until these land in order". It does NOT violate the graph rule as stated — the three spine tasks are strictly serial among themselves, which is what criterion 5 tests, and I verified there are no other bypass edges. It is also harmless in substance: AS-39 makes no Stripe calls by its own scope, so the custody-guard ordering property the spine exists to protect is intact and separately verified above, and the parallelism strictly helps the ready queue.
